text: =============================================================================== OAKRIDGE ACADEMY - OFFICIAL POLICY STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT =============================================================================== DOCUMENT CONTROL ---------------- Document ID: POL-2026-001 Effective Date: September 1, 2026 Target Audience: All Students, Staff, Parents, and Guardians Approved By: Office of the Principal 1. PHILOSOPHY & PURPOSE ----------------------- Oakridge Academy is dedicated to providing a safe, inclusive, and academically rigorous learning environment. This Code of Conduct outlines the expectations for student behavior to ensure respect, safety, responsibility, and academic integrity across all school activities, whether on campus, on school transport, or during school-sponsored

pect, safety, responsibility, and academic integrity across all school activities, whether on campus, on school transport, or during school-sponsored events. 2. CORE EXPECTATIONS -------------------- Students are expected to: - Treat all peers, faculty, staff, and visitors with dignity and respect. - Arrive on time, prepared, and ready to engage in class. - Demonstrate academic honesty in all assignments, quizzes, and exams. - Respect school property, as well as the personal belongings of others. - Follow all safety directives provided by school personnel. 3. ATTENDANCE & PUNCTUALITY --------------------------- - Regular Attendance: Absence from school requires a written note from a parent or medical professional within 24 hours of returning. - Tardiness: Unexcused tardiness to school or i

rom school requires a written note from a parent or medical professional within 24 hours of returning. - Tardiness: Unexcused tardiness to school or individual classes will result in demerits as follows: * 3 Unexcused Tardies = Parent notification * 5 Unexcused Tardies = After-school detention 4. ACADEMIC INTEGRITY --------------------- Academic dishonesty undermines the learning process. Prohibited behavior includes: - Plagiarism (presenting someone else's work, writing, or AI-generated output as your own). - Copying homework, lab reports, or test answers. - Assisting another student in engaging in academic dishonesty. Penalties: First offense results in a zero on the assignment and a parent conference. Subsequent offenses may lead to academic probation or suspension. 5. ACCEPTABLE USE OF

se results in a zero on the assignment and a parent conference. Subsequent offenses may lead to academic probation or suspension. 5. ACCEPTABLE USE OF TECHNOLOGY ------------------------------- - Personal Electronic Devices: Cell phones, smartwatches, and headphones must be turned off and stored in lockers or designated pouches during instructional hours (8:00 AM - 3:00 PM), unless explicit permission is granted by a teacher. - School Devices & Network: School computers and Wi-Fi networks must be used solely for educational purposes. Unauthorized access, streaming non-educational content, or attempting to bypass network filters is strictly forbidden. - Cyberbullying: Bullying, harassment, or intimidation using electronic communication (on or off campus) that creates a hostile environment a

rbidden. - Cyberbullying: Bullying, harassment, or intimidation using electronic communication (on or off campus) that creates a hostile environment at school will result in immediate administrative disciplinary action. 6. DRESS CODE GUIDELINES ------------------------ Students must wear the approved school uniform or adhere to the following standards: - Tops and bottoms must provide adequate coverage. - Clothing with vulgar language, offensive graphics, or references to illegal substances is prohibited. - Footwear appropriate for physical safety must be worn at all times (no flip-flops or unbuckled sandals during PE activities). 7. PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES & DANGEROUS ITEMS ------------------------------------------ The following items are strictly prohibited on school grounds, buses, and ev

D SUBSTANCES & DANGEROUS ITEMS ------------------------------------------ The following items are strictly prohibited on school grounds, buses, and events: - Tobacco products, e-cigarettes, vapes, and nicotine items. - Alcohol and illegal drugs or unprescribed medications. - Weapons, dangerous instruments, or replica weapons. Violation of this rule will result in immediate suspension, potential law enforcement notification, and expulsion proceedings where applicable. 8. DISCIPLINARY MATRIX & PROGRESSIVE CONSEQUENCES ------------------------------------------------- Oakridge Academy utilizes progressive discipline to encourage positive behavioral changes. Level 1 (Minor Infractions): - Classroom disruption, minor dress code violation, unexcused tardiness. - Actions: Verbal warning, teacher-

ral changes. Level 1 (Minor Infractions): - Classroom disruption, minor dress code violation, unexcused tardiness. - Actions: Verbal warning, teacher-student conference, parent notification. Level 2 (Moderate Infractions): - Repeated Level 1 infractions, academic dishonesty, disrespectful behavior to staff. - Actions: Loss of privileges, detention, parent-teacher conference. Level 3 (Severe Infractions): - Bullying/harassment, vandalism, fighting, possession of contraband. - Actions: In-school suspension (ISS), out-of-school suspension (OSS), board hearing, or expulsion. 9. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT & COMPLIANCE -------------------------------- Enrollment at Oakridge Academy signifies agreement to adhere to this Code of Conduct. Parents and students are required to sign and return the official ackno

ent at Oakridge Academy signifies agreement to adhere to this Code of Conduct. Parents and students are required to sign and return the official acknowledgment form during the first week of the academic year. =============================================================================== End of Document - Oakridge Academy Policy Department ===============================================================================

# =============================================================================== OAKRIDGE ACADEMY - OFFICIAL POLICY GRADING AND ASSESSMENT POLICY ## DOCUMENT CONTROL Document ID: POL-2026-002 Effective Date: September 1, 2026 Target Audience: Faculty, Students, Parents, and Academic Counselors Approved By: Office of the Principal & Academic Board 1. This policy outlines the principles and standards governing student evaluation, grading scales, assignment weightings, late work practices, and academic standing to ensure that grades accurately reflect student mastery of course standards. 2. rately reflect student mastery of course standards. 2. ASSESSMENT CATEGORIES & WEIGHTINGS To provide a comprehensive evaluation of academic progress, final term grades are calculated according to the following category breakdown: * Summative Assessments (50% of Final Grade): - Unit Exams, Comprehensive Projects, Term Essays, and Research Papers. * Formative Assessments (30% of Final Grade): - Quizzes, Lab Reports, Short Writing Assignments, and Structured Class Debates. * Classwork & Homework (20% of Final Grade): - Daily assignments, guided practice, preparation, and active learning participation. 4. # =============================================================================== OAKRIDGE ACADEMY - OFFICIAL POLICY STUDENT ATTENDANCE POLICY ## DOCUMENT CONTROL Document ID: POL-2026-003 Effective Date: September 1, 2026 Target Audience: All Students, Parents, Guardians, and Teaching Staff Approved By: Office of the Principal & Student Services 1. PHILOSOPHY & POLICY PURPOSE Oakridge Academy believes that regular, punctual school attendance is vital to academic achievement, social development, and building personal responsibility. This policy defines attendance requirements, distinguishes between excused and unexcused absences, and outlines progressive steps taken to address persistent truancy and tardiness. 2. DAILY SCHOOL HOURS * School Hours: 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM (Monday through Friday)

progressive steps taken to address persistent truancy and tardiness. 2. DAILY SCHOOL HOURS * School Hours: 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM (Monday through Friday) * Morning Homeroom Call: 8:05 AM * Tardiness Threshold: Arrival after 8:10 AM is recorded as an official Tardy. 3. ABSENCE CLASSIFICATIONS Absences are categorized into two types: A. Excused Absences An absence is classified as excused only when supported by valid documentation submitted within two (2) school days of the student's return. Valid reasons include: * Personal illness or medical emergency (doctor's note required for 3+ consecutive days). * Pre-arranged medical or dental appointments. * Bereavement or religious holiday observances. * Subpoenaed court appearances or family emergencies approved by administration. B. Unexcused Absence

* Bereavement or religious holiday observances. * Subpoenaed court appearances or family emergencies approved by administration. B. Unexcused Absences Any absence without proper parental or official notification, or for reasons not recognized by school guidelines (e.g., family vacations during school term without prior permission, sleeping in, missing the bus), will be recorded as unexcused. 4. NOTIFICATION & REPORTING PROCEDURES * Morning Absence Reporting: Parents/guardians must contact the Attendance Office by phone or email by 8:30 AM on the day of the absence. * Written Absence Excuse: Upon returning, the student must present a signed note or medical certificate to the administrative office detailing the reason and dates of absence. 5. TARDIENSS AND EARLY DEPARTURE * Tardiness: Arriv

ote or medical certificate to the administrative office detailing the reason and dates of absence. 5. TARDIENSS AND EARLY DEPARTURE * Tardiness: Arriving late disrupts the learning environment. * 3 Unexcused Tardies = Official Warning Notice to Parents. * 5 Unexcused Tardies = 1 Hour After-School Detention. * 10 Unexcused Tardies = Formal Parent-Principal Conference. * Early Dismissal: Requests for early departure must be submitted in writing before 8:00 AM. Students must be signed out by an authorized parent/guardian at the main office. 6. TRUANCY & ACADEMIC CONSEQUENCES * 5 Unexcused Absences: Triggers an Attendance Warning Letter sent home and a meeting with the academic counselor. * 10 Unexcused Absences: The student is placed on Attendance Probation. and a meeting with the academic counselor. * 10 Unexcused Absences: The student is placed on Attendance Probation. A formal intervention plan will be established. * Loss of Credit / Grade Reduction: A student who exceeds 15 unexcused absences in a single academic term may forfeit course credit for impacted subjects, subject to appeal. 7.
